title: Sick at Your Cabo Resort? Getting a Hotel Doctor Fast
description: Sick at your resort in Cabo? What happens when you call the front desk, how to get an English-speaking doctor to your room 24/7 for $199, and what it costs.

intro: It happens on more Cabo vacations than anyone admits: a fever on day two, a stomach bug after a seafood dinner, a child with an ear infection, or a hangover that will not let you out of bed. You are in a beautiful resort — and you need a doctor.
Here is what usually happens when you ask the front desk for help, what you can do instead, and what a hotel doctor visit costs with us.

sections.h2: What happens when you call the front desk
p: Most resorts can connect you with a doctor. Ask before the visit who the doctor is, how long they will take, what the visit costs in US dollars, and whether medicines are extra. A clear answer to those four questions is a good sign.

You can also call or message a medical service yourself. With us you talk directly to the team in English, get the price up front and a typical arrival time of 30–45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas and the Tourist Corridor, or up to about 60 minutes in San José del Cabo, Pedregal and Palmilla.

p: Chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, fainting, severe bleeding or a serious injury: call 911 and tell the front desk right away.

faq.q: Can a doctor come to my hotel room in Cabo?
faq.a: Yes. Our English-speaking doctors visit hotels, villas and yachts across Los Cabos 24/7 for $199 USD.

faq.q: How fast can a doctor get to my resort?
faq.a: Typically 30–45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas and the Tourist Corridor, and up to about 60 minutes in San José del Cabo, Pedregal and Palmilla.

faq.q: Will the resort let the doctor in?
faq.a: Yes. Give us your name and room number; the doctor checks in at the front desk or your villa gate under your name.

faq.q: Can I get medicine delivered to my room?
faq.a: Yes. The doctor can prescribe and our pharmacy delivers to your room, free on orders over $50 USD.
